## tangency-labs/solidcraft (https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft)
Description: SolidCraft: an open-source parametric 3D CAD application built in pure Rust. Desktop, web, and automation through MCP.
Homepage: https://solidcraft.io
Language: Rust; license: Apache-2.0; created 2026-10-07; last push 2026-11-27
Latest release: v0.50.0 (2026-11-26)
README (start):
SolidCraft

  An open-source parametric 3D CAD application built in pure Rust.
  Sketch, constrain, and build solids with a parametric feature timeline. Change a dimension
  and watch your model rebuild. Run it on your desktop, in your browser, or let AI agents
  model through the built-in MCP server.

  Website ·
  Download ·
  Try it in the browser ·
  Documentation ·
  
  Discord ·
  SolidCore

  
  
  
  
  
  
  

  
  

*A Raspberry Pi 4 case from an empty design: a sketch dimensioned with the board's parameters, extrude, fillet, shell, the rim rounded in one pick, an M2.5 standoff patterned on the 58 × 49 mm hole rectangle, port cut-outs, vent slots, "Pi 4" engraved in DejaVu Sans Bold and a PETG material defined in the design, with its mass in Properties, then height 24 → 32 mm in Parameters and it all rebuilds. 6× playback with the idle pauses cut. [Full video](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/screenshots/demo.mp4), recorded with the [demo script](examples/demo/record_ui.sh).*

## Download

- **Windows:** the [installer][windows-msi].
- **macOS:** the [disk image][macos-dmg] (Apple silicon and Intel).
- **Linux:** the [AppImage][linux-appimage], or a [Snap package][linux-snap]
  ([installation instructions][snap-install], including ARM64).
- **Web:** [try it in your browser][web-app], no install.

ARM64 and 32-bit builds, portable zip, .deb, .rpm, Flatpak and the other packages are on the
[downloads page](docs/downloads.md). The macOS app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by
Apple. The Windows files are unsigned for now ([code signing and privacy](https://docs.solidcraft.io/code-signing-policy.html)),
so SmartScreen may warn: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On SolidCraft 0.11 to 0.14, download once by hand; see
[updating](https://docs.solidcraft.io/guide/updates.html#updating-from-011-to-014).

## What works

Early but usable for simple parts: 75 of 76 public reference parts match their analytic or
FreeCAD-computed volume, area, centre of mass and bounding box ([oracle](docs/oracle.md)); the
other is a tracked bug.

- **Sketches and constraints:** lines, arcs, splines, text and more, solved by our own constraint solver, with parameter-driven dimensions.
- **Features:** extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, draft, holes, threads, patterns, mirror, split and combine on an editable parametric timeline.
- **Parameters and configurations** with unit-aware expressions.
- **Assemblies** with joints, motion studies, contact sets, interference and mass properties.
- **Sheet metal** with flanges, hems, fold/unfold and flat patterns. Choose how two edge flanges
  meet at a corner: **Butt**, **Partial overlap** or **Full overlap**.
- **Plastic enclosure features.**
- **Files:** STEP, IGES, 3MF, STL, OBJ and glTF in and out where supported, URDF export, `.sc` designs (`.solidcraft` files from earlier releases still open).
- **Desktop app, browser app, headless CLI and MCP server**, all running the same commands.

The full list is in [docs/capabilities.md](docs/capabilities.md) and [docs/features.md](docs/features.md);
status and plans are in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). See also [what people built](docs/showcase.md),
[3D mouse support](docs/3d-mouse.md) and the [architecture](docs/architecture.md).

## Build from source

```sh
cargo run --release -p solidcraft -- --sample      # desktop app with a sample part
cargo run --release -p solidcraft-cli -- commands  # the command registry
cargo run --release -p solidcraft-cli -- run examples/bracket.json --out bracket.step
cargo xtask ci                                     # fmt, clippy, tests, icons, assets, layers, wasm
```

More commands, the Windows cross-build and the browser build are in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md).

## AI agents (MCP)

`solidcraft-cli mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Headless it
runs its own design session, or with `--connect` it drives the running app so you can watch.
Claude Code: `claude mcp add solidcraft -- solidcraft-cli mcp`. If a terminal doesn't find
`solidcraft-cli` (older Windows installers don't put it on `PATH`), give its full path (by default
`"C:\\Program Files\\SolidCraft\\solidcraft-cli.exe"`). Tools, access rules and an example session:
[docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md).

## Scripts

A script is a JSON list of the same commands the UI runs, executed with `solidcraft-cli run`.
Format and example: [docs/scripts.md](docs/scripts.md). Pages can also be driven through the
[browser command API](docs/browser-api.md).

## Plugins (experimental desktop runtime)

Plugins add separately distributed behaviour without compiling that behaviour into SolidCraft.
The initial runtime loads **WebAssembly components**, explicitly requested by the user. Merely
installing a folder, enabling it in Preferences, or opening a design never executes plugin code.
The interface is experimental: WIT package `craft:plugin@0.2.0`, capability `commands@0.2` (plugins built for 0.1 still run). While
it is 0.x a minor version may break the one before it; the host refuses a plugin that needs a
capability it does not have, in plain words. Review a plugin again after an update. The desktop app and headless CLI use the same commands. Browser
execution, automatic downloads and updates, custom panels, and plugin-defined parametric feature
types are future work.

### Install and inspect

A package is a folder named after its id, containing `plugin.json` and a `.wasm` component.
Preferences > Plugins lists packages under the per-user data folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/SolidCraft/plugins`
on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/SolidCraft/plugins` on macOS, and
`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/solidcraft/plugins` on Linux. **Show in folder** opens this location.
You can also inspect and explicitly run a package in another folder. Nothing is downloaded by the host.

A minimal manifest looks like this. Plugin packages and examples are maintained outside this
repository, as specified in [the plugin RFC](docs/rfcs/0002-plugins.md).

```json
{
  "id": "example-box",
  "name": "Example box",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Create an ordinary editable box from dimensions.",
  "capabilities": ["commands@0.1"],
  "runtime": {
    "module": "plugin.wasm",
    "entries": ["make"],
    "commands": ["solid.box"],
    "limits": {"fuel": 10000000, "memory_mib": 64, "deadline_ms": 5000}
  }
}
```

Run `plugin.inspect` with `{"path":"/path/to/example-box"}` through the CLI's JSON scripts, MCP
`execute`, or the desktop control channel's `engine.execute`. It reads the manifest and component
without executing them, returning the declared commands, limits and an `approval` SHA-256 hash.
Review the author, code and declared rights before using that hash. Inspection does not approve a
package. Existing metadata-only packages remain listable but cannot run until they declare a runtime.

### Run explicitly

After reviewing the inspected package, execute:

```json
{
  "command": "plugin.run",
  "params": {
    "path": "/path/to/example-box",
    "approval": "",
    "entry": "make",
    "params": {"length": 20, "width": 10, "height": 3}
  }
}
```

For example, save that command in a JSON array and use `solidcraft-cli run commands.json`.
For the running desktop app, send it as the `command` and `params` of a standalone
`engine.execute` request (see [control protocol](docs/control-protocol.md)). The native host runs
it on a worker and keeps the window responsive. Stop or a design change discards the pending
result; the host does not automatically rerun external code. Desktop batches and scripts must send
`plugin.run` separately. Headless CLI scripts may include it as a normal command.

The hash binds **both the exact manifest bytes and the component bytes**, so an updated package
requires a fresh inspection and permission review. It is a content identity, not a signature or an
author's reputation. Agent chat asks before executing external plugin code. MCP and the control
channel keep their existing file scopes: allow the package folder explicitly where needed. Naming
a package never grants access to another folder.

### User resource ceilings

The invocation defaults remain **10,000,000 fuel, 64 MiB of guest memory and 5000 ms**.
The default host ceilings remain **100,000,000,000 fuel and 128 MiB**. A package can declare
larger fuel, memory, command host-call or guest compute time budgets, but execution is refused until you explicitly raise the host
ceilings and approve that exact package content. `plugin.inspect` is inert and reports the
requested limits, current `host_limits`, `within_host_limits` and any `limits_error` even when
a request is too large.

In the native GUI, open **Preferences > Plugins**, enter **Max plugin fuel**,
**Max plugin memory (MiB)**, **Max plugin host calls** and **Max plugin guest time (ms)**,
then choose **Apply** or **OK**. Enter also accepts the values;
**Cancel** reverts changes since the last Apply and **Restore defaults** resets this page.
The settings persist in your user preferences and do not travel with saved designs.

For standalone CLI or headless MCP sessions, create a UTF-8 JSON file, for example
`plugin-limits.json` containing:

```json
{"max_fuel": 200000000000, "max_memory_mib": 512, "max_host_calls": 2000, "max_deadline_ms": 120000}
```

Pass it explicitly when starting the process:

```text
solidcraft-cli --plugin-limits plugin-limits.json run inspect-plugin.json --results
solidcraft-cli --plugin-limits plugin-limits.json mcp --headless --allow-path /path/to/plugins
```

Missing fields use the original host ceilings. Connected desktop sessions use the GUI's
preferences; CLI settings cannot override them. Positive integer fuel, host-call and guest
deadline millisecond values up to `u64::MAX`
are accepted without rounding. Guest memory is limited to 4096 MiB by the current Wasm32 ABI;
that technical boundary requires a different runtime ABI to change. These settings do not change
a package's declared budget, executes it, adds permissions, or retries a failed invocation.
Review its manifest and component, obtain the content approval hash, and explicitly invoke it.
A changed manifest budget requires a fresh approval hash. Keep the selected ceilings within your
machine's available resources; they are limits on guest execution, not total SolidCraft memory
or native CAD work. The guest compute deadline pauses during native host work. Its command
ceiling defaults to 30 seconds, and the command host-call ceiling defaults to 256;
larger approved requests need these ceilings raised. Existing requests still default to
256 calls and 5 seconds of guest compute.

Standalone CLI runs and headless MCP use the plugins installed for the desktop app; approvals
given there last for the run. Add `--keep-plugin-approvals` to keep them between runs, shared
with the desktop app, so a plugin is installed and approved once, and `--plugins-dir DIR` to use
a separate set of plugins and approvals, for example in CI. List kept approvals with
`solidcraft-cli --keep-plugin-approvals exec plugin.grants` and take one back with
`solidcraft-cli --keep-plugin-approvals exec plugin.revoke '{"id":"PLUGIN_ID"}'`
([Headless use](docs/plugins.md#headless-use)).

### Permissions, results and saved designs

A plugin can call any command in the MCP catalog whose exact id its manifest lists. Commands that
reach past the open design are grouped: `file` (saving, exporting, importing, inserting from files,
libraries), `doc` (opening or switching designs), `app` (settings, window, diagnostics) and `plugin`
(inspecting or running plugins). Each group is refused unless the manifest requests it in
`runtime.permissions.command_groups` and the user grants it; this version has no grant UI yet.
Filesystem calls require matching manifest permissions and approved folder grants. The clock
requires its manifest permission; otherwise it returns a fixed epoch

### Your own 3D Parametric Modeler

[Website](https://www.freecad.org) •

Overview
--------

* **Freedom to build what you want**  FreeCAD is an open-source parametric 3D
modeler for designing real-life objects of any size. Parametric modeling lets
you modify a design by changing parameters in its model history.

* **Create 3D from 2D and back** FreeCAD lets you sketch geometry-constrained
2D shapes and use them as a base to build other objects. It also provides tools
to adjust dimensions and create high-quality production drawings from 3D models.

* **Designed for your needs** FreeCAD is designed to fit a wide range of uses
including product design, mechanical engineering and architecture,
whether you are a hobbyist, programmer, experienced CAD user, student or teacher.

* **Cross platform** FreeCAD runs on Windows, macOS and Linux operating systems.

* **Underlying technology**
    * **OpenCASCADE** A powerful geometry kernel, the most important component of FreeCAD
    * **Coin3D library** Open Inventor-compliant 3D scene representation model
    * **Python** FreeCAD offers a broad Python API
    * **Qt** Graphical user interface built with Qt

Installing
----------

Precompiled packages for stable releases are available for Windows, macOS and Linux on the
[latest releases page](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/releases/latest).

On most Linux distributions, FreeCAD is also directly installable from the 
software center application.

For weekly development releases visit the [releases page](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/releases/).

Other options are described on the [wiki Download page](https://wiki.freecad.org/Download).

Compiling
---------

See the [Developers Handbook – Getting Started](https://freecad.github.io/DevelopersHandbook/gettingstarted/)
for build instructions.

Reporting Issues
---------

To report an issue please:

- Consider posting to the [Forum](https://forum.freecad.org), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/w2cTKGzccC) channel, or [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/FreeCAD) to verify the issue; 
- Search the existing [issues](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues) for potential duplicates; 
- Use the most updated stable or [development versions](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/releases/) of FreeCAD; 
- Post version info from `Help > About FreeCAD > Copy to clipboard`; 
- Restart FreeCAD in safe mode `Help > Restart in safe mode` and try to reproduce the issue again. If the issue is resolved it can be fixed by deleting the FreeCAD config files.
- Start recording a macro `Macro > Macro recording...` and repeat all steps. Stop recording after the issue occurs and upload the saved macro or copy the macro code in the issue; 
- Post a Step-By-Step explanation on how to recreate the issue; 
- Upload an example file (FCStd as ZIP file) to demonstrate the problem; 

For more details see:

- [Bug Tracker](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues)
- [Reporting Issues and Requesting Features](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/new/choose)
- [Contributing](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Help Forum](https://forum.freecad.org/viewforum.php?f=3)

Contributing Code
-----------------

Read the [contribution process](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the
[contributor guidelines](contrib/guidelines/README.md) for practical advice on architecture,
code reuse, implementation, UI design, testing, and review. The guides link to relevant
sections of the [Developers Handbook](https://freecad.github.io/DevelopersHandbook/) and FEPs.

> [!NOTE]
The [FPA](https://fpa.freecad.org) offers developers the opportunity
to apply for a grant to work on projects of their choosing. Check
[jobs and funding](https://blog.freecad.org/jobs/) to know more.

Usage & Getting Help
--------------------

The FreeCAD wiki contains documentation on general usage and Python scripting.
View these pages for more information:

- [Getting started](https://wiki.freecad.org/Getting_started)
- [Features list](https://wiki.freecad.org/Feature_list)
- [Frequent questions](https://wiki.freecad.org/FAQ/en)
- [Workbenches](https://wiki.freecad.org/Workbenches)
- [Scripting](https://wiki.freecad.org/Power_users_hub)
- [Developers Handbook](https://freecad.github.io/DevelopersHandbook/)

The [FreeCAD forum](https://forum.freecad.org) is a great place
to find help and solve specific problems when learning to use FreeCAD.

## openscad/openscad (https://github.com/openscad/openscad)
Description: OpenSCAD - The Programmers Solid 3D CAD Modeller  
Homepage: https://www.openscad.org
Language: C++; license: NOASSERTION; created 2010-11-03; last push 2026-11-27
Latest release: openscad-2021.01 (2021-02-07)
README (start):
[](https://github.com/openscad/openscad/actions)
[](https://circleci.com/gh/openscad/openscad/tree/master)
[](https://scan.coverity.com/projects/2510)

[](https://kiwiirc.com/client/irc.libera.chat/#openscad)

# What is OpenSCAD?

OpenSCAD is a software for creating solid 3D CAD objects. It is free software and
available for Linux/UNIX, MS Windows and macOS.

Unlike most free software for creating 3D models (such as the famous
application Blender), OpenSCAD focuses on the CAD aspects rather than the
artistic aspects of 3D modeling. Thus this might be the application you are
looking for when you are planning to create 3D models of machine parts but
probably not the tool for creating computer-animated movies.

OpenSCAD is not an interactive modeler. Instead it is more like a
3D-compiler that reads a script file that describes the object and renders
the 3D model from this script file (see examples below). This gives you, the
designer, complete control over the modeling process and enables you to easily
change any step in the modeling process or make designs that are defined by
configurable parameters.

OpenSCAD provides two main modeling techniques: First there is constructive
solid geometry (aka CSG) and second there is extrusion of 2D outlines. As the data
exchange format for these 2D outlines Autocad DXF files are used. In
addition to 2D paths for extrusion it is also possible to read design parameters
from DXF files. Besides DXF files OpenSCAD can read and create 3D models in the
STL and OFF file formats.

# Contents

- [Getting Started](#getting-started)
- [Documentation](#documentation)
    - [Building OpenSCAD](#building-openscad)
        - [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
        - [Getting the source code](#getting-the-source-code)
        - [Building for macOS](#building-for-macos)
        - [Building for Linux/BSD](#building-for-linuxbsd)
        - [Building for Linux/BSD on systems with older or missing dependencies](#building-for-linuxbsd-on-systems-with-older-or-missing-dependencies)
        - [Building for Windows](#building-for-windows)
        - [Compilation](#compilation)

# Getting started

You can download the latest binaries of OpenSCAD at
. Install binaries as you would any other
software.

When you open OpenSCAD, you'll see three frames within the window. The
left frame is where you'll write code to model 3D objects. The right
frame is where you'll see the 3D rendering of your model.

Let's make a tree! Type the following code into the left frame:

```scad
cylinder(h = 30, r = 8);
```

Then render the 3D model by hitting F5. Now you can see a cylinder for
the trunk in our tree. Now let's add the bushy/leafy part of the tree
represented by a sphere. To do so, we will union a cylinder and a
sphere.

```scad
union() {
    cylinder(h = 30, r = 8);
    sphere(20);
}
```

But, it's not quite right! The bushy/leafy are around the base of the
tree. We need to move the sphere up the z-axis.

```scad
union() {
    cylinder(h = 30, r = 8);
    translate([0, 0, 40]) sphere(20);
}
```

And that's it! You made your first 3D model! There are other primitive
shapes that you can combine with other set operations (union,
intersection, difference) and transformations (rotate, scale,
translate) to make complex models! Check out all the other language
features in the [OpenSCAD
Manual](https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/OpenSCAD_User_Manual).

# Documentation

Have a look at the OpenSCAD Homepage (https://www.openscad.org/documentation.html) for documentation.

## Building OpenSCAD

To build OpenSCAD from source, follow the instructions for the
platform applicable to you below.

### Prerequisites

To build OpenSCAD, you need some libraries and tools. The version
numbers in brackets specify the versions which have been used for
development. Other versions may or may not work as well.

If you're using a newer version of Ubuntu, you can install these
libraries from aptitude. If you're using Mac, or an older Linux/BSD, there
are build scripts that download and compile the libraries from source.

## What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)? - Model Context Protocol

What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
Get started
What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
Copy page
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.
Using MCP, AI applications like Claude or ChatGPT can connect to data sources (e.g. local files, databases), tools (e.g. search engines, calculators) and workflows (e.g. specialized prompts)—enabling them to access key information and perform tasks.
Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications. Just as USB-C provides a standardized way to connect electronic devices, MCP provides a standardized way to connect AI applications to external systems.
What can MCP enable?
Agents can access your Google Calendar and Notion, acting as a more personalized AI assistant.
Claude Code can generate an entire web app using a Figma design.
Enterprise chatbots can connect to multiple databases across an organization, empowering users to analyze data using chat.
AI models can create 3D designs on Blender and print them out using a 3D printer.
Why does MCP matter?
Depending on where you sit in the ecosystem, MCP can have a range of benefits.
Developers: MCP reduces development time and complexity when building, or integrating with, an AI application or agent.
AI applications or agents: MCP gives them access to an ecosystem of data sources, tools and apps, which enhances their capabilities and improves the end-user experience.
End-users: MCP results in more capable AI applications or agents that can access user data and take actions on the user’s behalf when necessary.
Broad ecosystem support
MCP is an open protocol supported across a wide range of clients and servers. AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT, development tools like Visual Studio Code, Cursor, MCPJam, and many others all support MCP — making it easy to build once and integrate everywhere.
